newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Chevron to use Baku-Supsa pipeline for Tengiz oil.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to use Baku-Supsa pipeline for Tengiz oil.

text.p: U.S. oil giant Chevron Corp intends to use a pipeline running through Azerbaijan and Georgia to help get output from its Tengiz project in Kazakhstan to world markets, a company official said on Thursday.

Richard Matske, President of Chevron Overseas, said that the company would continue shipping part of its output by rail through the two Transcaucasus countries until repairs on the pipeline, running from the Azeri capital Baku to Georgia's Black Sea outlet at Supsa, are completed in 1998.
"We intend on continuing to transport oil through Georgia until we find a better alternative," he told reporters in the Georgian capital Tbilisi after meeting President Eduard Shevardnadze.
Matske said he was happy with the way its oil exports through Georgia were proceeding. The Tengiz output is first shipped by tanker accross the Caspian Sea to Baku and then loaded into railway cars.
Chevron has shipped 400,000 tonnes of oil along this route since the beginning of 1997.
He said a proposed underwater pipeline linking Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan looked to be promising geographically but that many questions associated with it needed to be worked out.
